title: 设置映射之后输入较快的情况下映射会失败

status.label: Reproduce rapid Alt-key remaps
status.detail: The mapping screenshot confirms Alt+U/I/O map to 7/8/9; the reporter says fast input sometimes leaks the original I or O.

judgment.rationale: The reporter gives a concrete Keyboard Manager mapping and contrasts slow versus fast input: while using Left Alt with U/I/O, slow input produces 7/8/9 but fast input sometimes leaves I or O unchanged. The attached screenshot was inspected and confirms the three relevant mappings. There are no comments, maintainer reproductions, or current-build results, so the first useful step is a controlled reproduction rather than a speculative code fix.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.87.1 and Keyboard Manager.
The report says Left Alt with U/I/O should produce 7/8/9, but rapid input sometimes produces 7/I/9 or 7/8/O.
The supplied mapping screenshot shows Alt+U to 7, Alt+I to 8, and Alt+O to 9 for all applications.
The issue currently has no comments or assignees.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the three mappings on current stable with slow and rapid Left-Alt input, recording whether the original letter event leaks through.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report is concrete enough to reproduce but does not establish whether the failure comes from modifier/key event ordering, input rollover, or another cause. No code change should be proposed before a maintainer verifies the sequence and current-build behavior.

issue_context.summary: Rapid Left-Alt input sometimes bypasses one of the configured U/I/O-to-7/8/9 mappings.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.87.1 and Keyboard Manager.
The reporter expects Left Alt+U/I/O to output 7/8/9.
The reporter says slow input works but rapid input sometimes leaves I or O unchanged.
The supplied screenshot confirms Alt+U to 7, Alt+I to 8, and Alt+O to 9 for all applications.
inferences: The reported failure may depend on the ordering or timing of adjacent modified key events, but the original sequence does not isolate a particular event transition.
issue_context.analysis: The screenshot removes ambiguity about the three relevant mappings. Reproduce the same held-modifier and key sequence at slow and fast rates before selecting an input-hook or state-management fix.
initial_investigation: Read the current issue body and labels; the discussion has no comments or maintainer reproduction.
Inspected the supplied mapping screenshot and confirmed the Left-Alt U/I/O mappings to 7/8/9.

information_gaps.information: Whether the fast-input failure persists on current stable and the exact outputs from a controlled U-then-I-then-O sequence while Left Alt remains held
information_gaps.why_needed: The report is from 0.87.1 and describes intermittent results without isolating which key event or release order is missed.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Repeat the reported sequence on current stable, first slowly and then quickly, and record the output for each key.

actions.label: Compare slow and rapid Left-Alt remaps

reproduce.title: Check rapid sequential Left-Alt key remapping
reproduce.version_requirement: Current stable; the issue was reported on PowerToys 0.87.1
prerequisites: Left Alt available as a physical modifier
setup: Configure Left Alt+U to 7, Left Alt+I to 8, and Left Alt+O to 9 for all applications.
steps: Hold Left Alt and press U, I, and O slowly one at a time; confirm the output.
Repeat the same sequence while pressing the keys rapidly without releasing Left Alt.
Record whether any original I or O character appears instead of 8 or 9.
Repeat each chord individually to compare with the sequential input.
reproduce.expected_result: Every configured chord produces its mapped digit at both slow and rapid input rates, without leaking the original letter.
